NOTE: We just did production setup

// npm init
// Initializes a new Node.js project and creates package.json file

// Empty folders GitHub pe push nahi hote
// Isliye hum .gitkeep file daalte hain taaki folder track ho sake Ex: public\temp\.gitkeep

// .gitignore
// Isme hum wo files likhte hain jo GitHub pe upload nahi karni
// Example: node_modules, .env, logs, etc.
// Ye sensitive data aur auto-generated files ko ignore karta hai

// Gitignore generators
// Online tools jo automatically important ignore rules generate kar dete hain

// Environment Variables (.env)
// Sensitive data (API keys, DB URLs) store karte hain
// Ye directly system se access hote hain (process.env) for better security

// Nodemon
// Server ko automatically restart karta hai jab code me changes hote hain

// Dependencies vs Dev Dependencies
// dependencies: production me bhi use hoti hain
// devDependencies: sirf development ke time use hoti hain
// Example:
// npm i nodemon        -> dependency
// npm i -D nodemon     -> dev dependency (hmne ye kiya)

// package.json scripts change for nodemon
// "scripts": {
//   "dev": "nodemon index.js"
// }

// Middleware
// Request aur response ke beech me run hone wala function
// Example use: authentication, logging, validation

// Prettier (Code Formatter)
// Team me consistent code formatting ke liye use hota hai
// Install as dev dependency:
// npm i -D prettier

// .prettierrc
// Prettier configuration file (rules define karte hain)

// .prettierignore
// Jin files/folders par prettier apply nahi karna unhe yahan likhte hain

#V7(Database Connection)-------------------------------------

// How to connect to MongoDB Atlas (Correct + Complete Steps)

// 1. Go to MongoDB Atlas and login/signup
//    - Create Organization (name anything)
// 2. Create Project
//    - Click "New Project" → give name → create
// 3. Create Cluster (Deployment)
//    - Choose FREE tier (M0)
//    - Select cloud provider (AWS recommended)
//    - Choose nearest region (low latency)
//    - Click "Create Cluster"
// ⚠️ Wait for cluster to be fully created (1–3 min)
// 4. Setup Database User (IMPORTANT)
//    - Go to "Database Access"
//    - Add new user (username + strong password)
//    - Role: "Read and write to any database"
// 5. Setup Network Access (IMPORTANT)
//    - Go to "Network Access"
//    - Add IP: 0.0.0.0/0 (allow all)
//    - OR add your current IP (more secure)
// ⚠️ If you skip step 4 or 5 → connection will FAIL
// 6. Get Connection String
//    - Go to "Database" → Click "Connect"
//    - Select "Drivers" (NOT Compass for code)
//    - Choose Node.js
//    - Copy connection string
// Example:
// mongodb+srv://username:<password>@cluster0.xxxx.mongodb.net/
// 7. Replace <password> with your actual password
// 8. Add Database Name (BEST PRACTICE)
// mongodb+srv://username:password@cluster0.xxxx.mongodb.net/myDatabase
// 9. Use in your code (Mongoose or MongoDB driver)
// Done ✅

V8(Custom api response and error handling)-------------------

jv v Middleware use krte hain to most of the time app.use k through krte, app.use hm tb use krte jb middleware use krna ho ya to koi configuration settings krni hai

npm i cookie-parser cors

// Middleware ek function hota hai jo request aur response ke beech me execute hota hai
// Yeh request ko process karta hai before reaching the final route handler
// Yeh middleware har incoming request ko log karega
// next() call karna zaroori hai warna request yahin ruk jayegi

#Example:       ┌───────────────┐
                │   /instagram  │
                └──────┬────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
            (err,req,res,next)
                 ┌─────────┐
                 │         │
                 └───┬─┬───┘
                     │ │
         ┌───────────┘ └───────────┐
         ▼                         ▼
┌──────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────┐
│ check if user logged │   │ check if user admin  │
└──────────┬───────────┘   └──────────┬───────────┘
           │                          │
           └──────────┬───────────────┘
                      ▼
          ┌──────────────────────┐
          │  res.send("hitesh")  │
          └──────────────────────┘

V9(Hooks and JWT)-------------------------------------------------

user model me hm id likhte nhi as mongodb jb model save krta hai to ek unique id generate kr k deta hi hai ,bson data me save krta hai json data me nhi krta

plugin hook ek extra feature add karne wala tool hota hai, jaise phone me app install karne se naye features milte hain; waise hi mongoose me plugin lagane se schema me nayi functionality add ho jati hai, simple words me plugin ek upgrade ya extra feature hota hai.

mongoose-aggregate-paginate-v2 ek aisa tool hai jo bade data ko chhote parts yani pages me divide karta hai, jaise page 1 me pehle 10 items aur page 2 me agle 10; jab data bahut zyada hota hai to sab ek saath bhejna slow ho jata hai, isliye ye aggregation query ka result lekar automatically usko page-wise tod deta hai jahan query batati hai kya data chahiye aur options me page number aur per page kitna data chahiye.

Aggregation pipeline simple language me ek process hai jisme data ko step-by-step handle kiya jata hai—har step (stage) me kuch kaam hota hai jaise filter karna, sort karna, ya group karna, aur last me final result milta hai; matlab data ek pipeline se guzarta hai jahan har stage usko thoda modify karta hai.

bcrypt aur JWT dono authentication me use hote hain jahan bcrypt password ko secure banane ke liye use hota hai—ye password ko hash karke database me store karta hai taaki original password safe rahe—aur JWT login ke baad ek token generate karta hai jo user har request ke saath bhejta hai; server is token ko verify karke user ko authenticate karta hai, is tarah bcrypt password security handle karta hai aur JWT login ke baad user verification manage karta hai; inhe use karne ke liye install karte hain: npm i bcrypt jsonwebtoken.

jwt ek bearer token hai jo isko bear krte ye use data bhej deta ek trh se chavi ki trh hai iske pass token uske pass data

// 🔐 Tokens (Access + Refresh)
// Access token short-lived hota hai aur har request me bheja jata hai (Authorization header)
// Ye user ko authenticate karta hai aur isme basic user data hota hai (id, email, etc.)

// Refresh token long-lived hota hai aur sirf tab use hota hai jab access token expire ho jaye
// Ye minimal data (sirf user id) rakhta hai aur naya access token generate karne ke kaam aata hai

//Access token short time ke liye valid hota hai, aur jab expire ho jata hai tab refresh token use karke bina dobara login/email diye naya access token generate kar lete hain, jisse user ka session continuous bana rehta hai.

pre hook mongoose me ek function hota hai jo kisi operation (jaise save, delete, update) ke hone se pehle automatically run hota hai, iska use tab karte hain jab hume data ko store hone se pehle modify ya check karna ho—jaise password ko save hone se pehle hash karna—matlab main action se pehle extra kaam karna.

V11(HTTP)---------------------------------------------------------

HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer data between a browser and a server but is not secure because it sends data in plain text, making it vulnerable to interception and attacks, whereas HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is the secure version that uses SSL/TLS encryption to protect data, ensuring that the information transmitted remains private and safe from hackers, and it adds an extra layer of security over HTTP, which is why it is commonly used for sensitive activities like online transactions and logins.

URI → sabka parent term, kisi bhi resource ka identifier
URL → resource ka location + access method (e.g., https://...)
URN → resource ka sirf naam, location nahi (permanent ID)

📌 HTTP Headers
* HTTP headers = metadata (data ke baare me info)
* Ye request & response ke saath send hote hain
🔹 Kaam kya hai?
* Data ka format batana (Content-Type)
* Authentication (Authorization)
* Caching & control
🔹 Format
Key: Value
Example: Content-Type: application/json
🔹 Types
* Request Headers → client se
* Response Headers → server se
* Representation Headers → format/encoding
* Payload Headers → data info
🔹 One Line
Headers = instructions + extra info about data

📌 Most Common HTTP Headers (Easy)
* Accept → client kya type ka response chahta hai (e.g. application/json)
* User-Agent → client/browser info
* Authorization → user authentication (token etc.)
* Content-Type → data ka format kya hai
* Cookie → user/session data store karne ke liye
* Cache-Control → caching control
📌 CORS Headers
* Access-Control-Allow-Origin → kaun request kar sakta hai
* Access-Control-Allow-Credentials → cookies/auth allow ya nahi
* Access-Control-Allow-Methods → kaunse methods allowed (GET, POST etc.)
📌 Security Headers
* Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy → resources embed rules
* Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy → window/tab security control
* Content-Security-Policy → kaunse resources load ho sakte hain
* X-XSS-Protection → XSS attack protection
🔹 One Line
👉 Ye headers security, access aur data handling control karte hain

📌 HTTP Methods 
* HTTP methods = server ke saath interact karne ke actions
🔹 Methods
* GET → data fetch karna
* HEAD → sirf headers (body nahi aata)
* OPTIONS → kaunse operations allowed hain
* TRACE → same request wapas milti hai (testing)
* DELETE → data/resource delete karna
* PUT → poora resource replace karna
* POST → naya data add karna / interact karna
* PATCH → thoda part update karna
🔹 One Line
👉 HTTP Methods = server ko batate hain kya action perform karna hai

📌 HTTP Status Codes
* Status codes = server ka response batate hain (request ka kya hua)
🔹 Categories
* 1xx → Informational (process chal raha hai)
* 2xx → Success (request successful)
* 3xx → Redirection (dusri jagah bheja gaya)
* 4xx → Client Error (galti client ki)
* 5xx → Server Error (galti server ki)
🔹 Common Codes
* 100 → Continue
* 102 → Processing
* 200 → OK
* 201 → Created
* 202 → Accepted
* 307 → Temporary Redirect
* 308 → Permanent Redirect
* 400 → Bad Request
* 401 → Unauthorized
* 402 → Payment Required
* 404 → Not Found
* 500 → Internal Server Error
* 504 → Gateway Timeout
🔹 One Line
👉 Status codes batate hain request ka result kya hua

V18(Subscription Model)---------------------------------------------------------

Subscription schema:
subscriber → userId
channel → userId

Note:
subscriber bhi ek user hai
channel bhi ek user hai (jo apna channel chalata hai)

Har document = ek subscription

-----------------------------------
Users → A, B, C, D, E
Channels → CAC, HCC, FCC
-----------------------------------

Subscriptions (documents):

[A] ─────▶ [CAC]
[B] ─────▶ [CAC]
[C] ─────▶ [HCC]
[D] ─────▶ [FCC]
[C] ─────▶ [CAC]

-----------------------------------
Channel ke subscribers kaise nikaale?
-----------------------------------

Example: CAC

[A] ─▶ CAC
[B] ─▶ CAC
[C] ─▶ CAC

→ Total subscribers of CAC = 3

-----------------------------------
User ne kitne channels subscribe kiye?
-----------------------------------

Example: C

C ─▶ HCC
C ─▶ CAC

→ C subscribed to 2 channels

-----------------------------------
Final concept:
-----------------------------------
Count = number of documents matching condition

channel = X → subscribers count
subscriber = X → subscribed channels count

V20(Aggregation pipeline)-------------------------------------------------------

/*
🔥 MongoDB + Mongoose ObjectId & Aggregation (FULL CLEAR NOTES)

1. MongoDB _id:

- Har document ka unique field hota hai: _id
- Type: ObjectId (ye string nahi hota, special BSON type hota hai)

------------------------------------------------------------

2. Mongoose behavior (IMPORTANT):

- Agar tu _id nahi deta → Mongoose automatically ObjectId bana deta hai
- Normal queries me (find, findById, findOne):

  👉 Agar tu string pass kare:
     "661a8f3c9b1e8c001234abcd"

  👉 Mongoose internally convert kar deta hai:
     new ObjectId("661a8f3c9b1e8c001234abcd")

Example:
User.findById(req.user._id) ✅ (string hone pe bhi chal jata hai)

------------------------------------------------------------

3. req.user._id ka scene (REAL CONFUSION):

- JWT / middleware ke through jo req.user aata hai:
  
  👉 usme _id mostly STRING hoti hai

Kyu?
- JWT JSON me store hota hai → ObjectId string me convert ho jata hai

Example:
req.user._id = "661a8f3c9b1e8c001234abcd"  // string

------------------------------------------------------------

4. Aggregation Pipeline (MAIN TRAP):

- Aggregation = raw MongoDB
- Yaha Mongoose ka auto-conversion nahi hota ❌

Wrong:
{
  $match: {
    _id: req.user._id   // ❌ string vs ObjectId mismatch
  }
}

👉 MongoDB bolega:
"mere paas ObjectId hai, tu string de raha hai"

------------------------------------------------------------

5. Correct way (MANDATORY):

import mongoose from "mongoose";

{
  $match: {
    _id: new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(req.user._id)  // ✅ correct
  }
}

👉 Ab string → ObjectId convert ho gaya
👉 Match mil jayega ✅

------------------------------------------------------------

6. $lookup ka common bug:

Problem:
- localField → string
- foreignField (_id) → ObjectId

👉 Result: empty array ❌

Example (WRONG):
{
  $lookup: {
    from: "users",
    localField: "user",      // string
    foreignField: "_id",     // ObjectId
    as: "userDetails"
  }
}

Fix:
- Schema me ObjectId use karo:
  user: {
    type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId,
    ref: "User"
  }

YA

- aggregation me convert karo

------------------------------------------------------------

7. GOLDEN RULE:

👉 find / findById → Mongoose auto convert karega ✅
👉 aggregate → sab manually karna padega ❌

------------------------------------------------------------

8. ONE LINE MEMORY:

👉 "Aggregation = raw MongoDB → no magic → convert everything manually"

------------------------------------------------------------

9. FINAL REAL-WORLD SUMMARY:

- req.user._id → string
- MongoDB _id → ObjectId
- findById → chal jayega
- aggregate → fail hoga (agar convert nahi kiya)

👉 Solution:
ALWAYS use:
new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(req.user._id)

------------------------------------------------------------
*/
